sect1.title: File Downloads
sect1.para: On each page for most of the packages, there are download links for key files needed by the installation process. Usually, these are tarballs of source code and patches to solve various issues. If you are following GLFS right after LFS or MLFS, you probably don't have the tools necessary on the LFS target to download any of the necessary files, or a network connection. If you do, GLFS can be treated like BLFS in that you can download files as you go, but can be pretty inconvenient.
In whatever case, you may want to download every file in bulk.

Firstly, whatever directory you choose to download to is up to you. But you should do it in an environment that both has and a network connection. If you'll follow GLFS in a chroot, you could download the files in $LFS/sources outside the chroot, then follow GLFS in the chroot. If you'll follow GLFS in a TTY, you could download the files on another distribution, put them on a storage device, and hook up the storage device to the LFS target so the files are accessible. You could also do a combination of all of the above or something else. All of that is if you don't have and a network connection on the LFS target. If you do, you can follow the bulk downloading process normally wherever you want.
Download the Wget file list, then download all the files listed in it:

note.para: If you rendered GLFS yourself, you may want to use the version of wget-list that came with the render. In that case, copy to the directory you want to download the files to. file:// or something else may be prefixed in the link. Make sure to delete that prefix first to ensure the file gets copied. The link will point to an online source if you didn't render the book. The link should be unique to your render.

sect1.para: To verify every file has been downloaded, you can run the following:

screen.userinput: for file in $(grep -v '^#' wget-list); do if [ ! -f $(basename $file) ]; then echo "$(basename $file) NOT found" fi done

sect1.para: If every file got downloaded, there should be no output from the above commands.

important.para: The files for &nvidia; and &cuda; are not downloaded from the above process as they are big files and would total to about 9G on their own. However, files for packages like are downloaded. You may wish to download the files now ahead of time. To do so, first read , decide on a major NVIDIA revision, then download the files in each page within that revision section.

Files for a package bundle like and will also not be downloaded by the above instructions. They instead get downloaded when you reach those package bundles, in which the tools to download them should become available.
